itc_eligibility.description: Eligibility conditions for claiming Input Tax Credit (ITC) on business purchases.
conditions: The buyer must possess a valid tax invoice or debit note issued by a registered supplier.
The buyer must have received the underlying goods and/or services.
The tax charged on the supply must have been paid to the government by the supplier.
The buyer must have filed their monthly/quarterly GST return (Form GSTR-3B).
The supplier must upload the invoice to the GST portal, appearing in the buyer's Form GSTR-2B.

blocked_credits.description: Purchases for which Input Tax Credit (ITC) is strictly blocked and cannot be claimed, even if used for business purposes.

categories.Motor Vehicles: ITC is blocked for motor vehicles carrying 13 or fewer passengers unless used for passenger transportation, goods transportation, or driving school training.
categories.Food, Beverages & Catering: ITC is blocked on food and beverages, outdoor catering, beauty treatment, health services, cosmetic and plastic surgery unless used for making outward supplies of the same category.
categories.Employee Welfare & Benefits: ITC is blocked on club memberships, fitness/health center memberships, travel benefits to employees on vacation (LTA), and life/health insurance, unless mandatory by law for the employer to provide.
categories.Personal Consumption: ITC is blocked on any goods or services used for personal consumption rather than business use.
categories.Lost, Stolen or Gifted Goods: ITC is blocked on goods lost, stolen, destroyed, written off, or disposed of by way of gift or free samples.
categories.Works Contract Services: ITC is blocked on works contract services for construction of an immovable property (except plant and machinery) on own account.

expense_category_rates.description: Default GST rates applied to inward expense categories when the organisation is GST-registered. Rates follow common Indian GST classifications for services and goods. Place of supply (intra vs inter-state) decides CGST+SGST vs IGST.

Utilities.note: Many utility-related supplies; electricity itself may be outside GST depending on supplier invoice.

Salaries.note: Salary is not a GST supply.

Travel.note: Passenger transport / travel agency rates vary; default 5% for common travel expenses unless invoice shows otherwise.

Employee Welfare.note: GST may apply on the purchase; ITC is often blocked under Sec 17(5).

Food & Beverages.note: Restaurant / food supplies often 5% without ITC; ITC usually blocked.

Motor Vehicles.note: Motor vehicles often 28%; ITC frequently blocked under Sec 17(5).

turnover_under_400cr.description: Domestic company where turnover in the previous year did not exceed Rs. 400 crore.

turnover_over_400cr.description: Domestic company where turnover in the previous year exceeded Rs. 400 crore.

section_115baa.description: Concessional tax rate option for domestic companies without claiming specified incentives/deductions.
section_115baa.conditions: No deductions allowed (under sections 10AA, 32(1)(iia) additional depreciation, 32AD, 33AB, 35 scientific research, or chapter VI-A except 80JJAA).

section_115bab.description: Concessional tax rate option for new manufacturing domestic companies incorporated on or after Oct 1, 2019.
section_115bab.conditions: Must commence production before March 31, 2024. No deductions or exemptions allowed.

section_80jjaa.title: Deduction for Employment of New Employees
section_80jjaa.description: A tax incentive allowing a deduction of 30% of the additional employee cost (emoluments paid to new employees) for 3 consecutive assessment years.
conditions: The business is not formed by splitting up or reconstruction of an existing business.
The number of employees must increase by at least 10% (or 10 employees for smaller firms, or any increase in the first year).
The monthly gross salary of the new employee must not exceed Rs. 25,000.
The employee must have been employed for at least 240 days in the financial year (or 150 days in the case of apparel, footwear, or leather manufacturing).
The employee must participate in the Employee Provident Fund (EPF) scheme.
The tax audit report (Form 10DA) must be filed by a Chartered Accountant.

depreciation_rates.description: Depreciation allowance computed using the Written Down Value (WDV) method on block of assets.

deadlines.title: GST GSTR-1 Filing
deadlines.description: Details of outward supplies of goods or services. Due on the 11th of the succeeding month.

deadlines.title: GST GSTR-3B Filing
deadlines.description: Monthly summary return and payment of tax. Due on the 20th of the succeeding month.
required_documents: GSTR-2B matching statement for Input Tax Credit

deadlines.title: TDS Payment Deposit
deadlines.description: Monthly deposit of Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) for salaries, contractor fees, rent, etc. Due by the 7th of the succeeding month.

deadlines.title: Advance Tax Installment 1
deadlines.description: Payment of 15% of estimated tax liability for the financial year.

deadlines.title: Advance Tax Installment 2
deadlines.description: Payment of 45% of estimated tax liability for the financial year.

deadlines.title: Advance Tax Installment 3
deadlines.description: Payment of 75% of estimated tax liability for the financial year.

deadlines.title: Advance Tax Installment 4
deadlines.description: Payment of 100% of estimated tax liability for the financial year.
